title: Expand file-operand globs on Windows in each command
story: Since the previous PR quotes every glob-bearing argument so MSYS children no longer expand it, `rtk ls *.rs` from PowerShell or cmd reaches the child as a literal name and fails. This PR adds a Windows-only expander and has each command expand only its own file operands, so patterns and flags stay literal.

nodes.label: ls
nodes.summary: Expands free positional paths before building the ls child args
nodes.detail: `build_child_args` passes the free positionals through `expand_operands`. Flags and values are untouched. It also switches from `child_args` to `ChildCommand::args`.

nodes.label: wc
nodes.summary: Expands every non-option argument except the --files0-from value
nodes.detail: New `expand_file_operands` skips `--files0-from` values (including the abbreviated `--f`) and expands everything after `--`. Unit tests use a marker expander to check which arguments count as operands.

nodes.label: grep / rg
nodes.summary: Expands only path positionals once at the top of run
nodes.detail: `expand_path_operands` reads paths the same way as `extract_pattern_path` (all positionals when `-e`, `-f` or `rg --files` supply the pattern). Passthrough, streaming and capture modes all see the expanded args, while the tracked command stays as typed.

nodes.label: find
nodes.summary: Expands only starting points, keeping the expression literal
nodes.detail: `dispatch` expands `rest[..split]`. `-name '*.rs'` and the legacy pattern form stay as written, and the verbatim `-exec`/`-delete` path is rebuilt from the expanded starting points.

nodes.label: operand_glob
nodes.summary: Windows-only glob, brace and tilde expander for file operands
nodes.detail: `expand_operands` follows the old `globify` rules: per-component matching, case-sensitive, dotfiles need a literal dot, `{a,b}` and `~` expand, and no match keeps the operand. `\` is a separator, and an operand naming an existing path is never expanded. On Unix it passes operands through.

nodes.label: ChildCommand
nodes.summary: Quotes glob arguments so MSYS children receive them literally
nodes.detail: It comes from the base PR and is unchanged here. It still quotes any argument with glob characters, which is why operands must be expanded before reaching it.

nodes.label: Filesystem / cwd
nodes.summary: Current directory and home used to resolve patterns
nodes.detail: The expander calls `user_dirs::current_dir()` and `home()`, then reads directories with `read_dir` and `symlink_metadata` to find matches.

edges.label: free positionals
edges.caption: ls hands its free positional paths to the expander.

edges.label: file operands
edges.caption: wc expands each non-option argument, skipping the --files0-from value.

edges.label: path positionals
edges.caption: grep and rg expand only their path arguments, not the pattern.

edges.label: starting points
edges.caption: find expands its starting points and leaves the expression literal.

edges.label: read_dir, home
edges.caption: The expander matches each path component against directory entries and resolves a leading ~.

edges.label: expanded args
edges.caption: The expanded names go to ChildCommand, which quotes any that still hold glob characters.

edges.label: expanded args
edges.caption: wc spawns its child with the expanded file list.

edges.label: engine_command
edges.caption: grep or rg is spawned with the expanded paths and the literal pattern.

edges.caption: find is spawned with the expanded starting points and the unchanged expression.
